title: The Presentation in the Temple: Fourth Joyful Mystery
summary: Pray the Fourth Joyful Mystery page by page: the story of the Presentation in the Temple, the Gospel, the decade prayers, and a quiet reflection.
coverAlt: Mantegna's painting of the Presentation: Mary holds the child Jesus over the Temple altar.

pages.title: The Presentation in the Temple
pages.body: Mary and Joseph carried the baby Jesus to the Temple in Jerusalem to present him to the Lord. Old Simeon took Jesus in his arms and praised God, and he told Mary that a sword would pierce her heart. As we pray this decade, we learn to offer our days to God, even when it costs us something.
pages.imageAlt: Mantegna's painting of the Presentation: Mary holds the child Jesus over the Temple altar.

evidence.claim: Original child-friendly meditation on the mystery; the mystery and its traditional day follow the standard Rosary order.

pages.title: From the Gospel
pages.body:
God's Word tells us this mystery. From the Gospel according to Luke, chapter 2 (Douay-Rheims Bible):

“He also took him into his arms, and blessed God, and said: Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word in peace; Because my eyes have seen thy salvation, Which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples: A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. … And thy own soul a sword shall pierce, that, out of many hearts, thoughts may be revealed.”

(Luke 2:22-35)

evidence.claim: Scripture quotation reproduced word for word from the Douay-Rheims 1899 American Edition (public domain); verse numbers omitted for reading aloud and ellipses mark skipped verses.

pages.title: Praying the Decade
pages.body:
We announce the mystery: The Presentation in the Temple, the Fourth Joyful Mystery. Then we pray one decade of the Rosary, holding this scene in our hearts.

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen. (We pray the Hail Mary ten times, once for each bead of the decade.)

Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit; as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell; lead all souls to Heaven, especially those in most need of Thy mercy.

evidence.claim: The Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be and Fatima prayers use the standard formulas printed across this site.

pages.title: The Fruit of This Mystery: Obedience and self-offering
pages.body:
This mystery grows the fruit of obedience and self-offering. Simeon waited his whole life to see Jesus. Is there something good you are waiting for? Offer the waiting to God.

Let us pray: Lord Jesus, teach us to offer you our whole lives, as Mary and Joseph offered you in the Temple. Amen. Our Lady of the Rosary, pray for us.

evidence.claim: Original reflection and closing prayer; the fruit of the mystery follows the traditional list used across this site.
